title: Ordered orthogonal arrays and nets of any kind (not necessarily linear) with the largest number of factors
keeper: W. Ch. Schmid and R. Schuerer, MinT, the database of optimal net, code, OA and OOA parameters (mint.sbg.ac.at)
revision: table.php (types Linear/Digital and Bound (linear/digital); every base 2 to 256 and every depth 1 to 8 and net; m from 3 to 51, k from 3 to 52), read 14 Nov 2026 11:27-11:39 UTC; MinT's database was last updated 2024-09-05; two pages (base 2, depths 6 and 7) were cut by the server above k = 27 and only their complete rows are used

template.title: Ordered orthogonal array of any kind with {b}^{m} runs, depth {T}, strength {k}
template.statement: Find an ordered orthogonal array (any array, linear or not) with {b}^{m} runs over {b} symbols, depth {T} and strength {k} that has as many factors as possible. Depth 1 is an orthogonal array; depth net is a ({m}-{k}, {m}, s)-net in base {b}, written by the first {k} base-{b} digits of each coordinate.
template.submission: Text file: the {b}^{m} runs, one per line, each the symbols (below {b}) of every factor in turn, {T} coordinates per factor in order of depth ({k} for depth net); see checkers/oa_check.py.

score: the number of factors (larger is better)
best_text: The best known object of any kind in MinT has {best} factors; an array with more factors improves it.
bound_source: MinT's bound for arbitrary objects in the same cell
holder_unknown: the construction and its source are on the cell's page at MinT
holder_sources: the tables list values only; each cell's page names its construction
open_rule: every cell with 3 <= k <= m of the MinT tables for arbitrary objects whose best known object has fewer factors than MinT's bound for arbitrary objects, with at most 2^16 runs, whose check takes at most 2^33 steps, and whose best known value or bound differs from the linear cell's (field linear: the linear cell's values)
left_out: 6871 solved cells; 57752 open cells with more than 2^16 runs; 239 open cells whose check would take more than 2^33 steps; 249 open cells whose best known value and bound equal those of the linear cell (asked in ordered-orthogonal-array); cells with k < 3 or m < k
